name: AngelTrax Mobile Video Surveillance Solutions

profile.address: 119, South Woodburn Drive, Dothan, Houston County, Alabama, 36305
profile.reading:
The building at this address, 119 South Woodburn Drive in Dothan, Alabama, is the corporate headquarters of AngelTrax, a manufacturer of mobile video surveillance and fleet-safety systems for school buses, mass transit, locomotives, and commercial fleets -- not a purpose-built or commercial data center in the ordinary sense this registry otherwise documents. AngelTrax's own site describes a company, operating since 2006, that builds in-vehicle cameras, stop-arm safety systems for school buses, driver-behavior analytics, and fleet-monitoring hardware, with roughly 250,000 active systems in the field worldwide and about 30,000 shipped annually. That same page does state that AngelTrax maintains what it calls a "SOC 2 Type II-compliant data center" at this headquarters location, describing it as the secure hosted video and data infrastructure behind its CJIS-compliant video-storage product for customers' recorded footage.

That claim is almost certainly why this location was tagged as a data center in the underlying map data, and it should be taken at face value as far as it goes: AngelTrax does host customer video data from company-owned infrastructure here. But it is an enterprise-private facility built to serve AngelTrax's own product, not a wholesale or colocation data center that leases capacity to outside tenants, and nothing in AngelTrax's public materials describes dedicated generator plant, a raised-floor server hall, or other purpose-built data center construction distinct from an office building with a server room inside it. No zoning case, building permit, or utility record specific to a data-center-scale power or cooling buildout has been found for this Woodburn Drive address, which is consistent with a corporate office housing IT infrastructure sized to the company's own hosted-video workload rather than a facility built around server capacity as its primary purpose.

AngelTrax itself is a real, active company serving the pupil-transportation and fleet-safety markets nationally from this Dothan base, and the hosted-video service it offers customers is a legitimate part of its business. The relevant point for this registry is narrower: this entry documents an enterprise's own internal hosting footprint attached to its headquarters, not a facility that markets data center space, and readers researching commercial data center capacity in the Dothan, Alabama area should not treat this listing as evidence of purpose-built colocation infrastructure at this address. Enterprise-private server rooms like this one are common and rarely publish specifications, because they were never built to be marketed -- that absence of a public spec sheet is itself the expected signature of this category of facility, not a research gap.

reading: AngelTrax, the operating brand of IVS, Inc., is a Dothan, Alabama transportation safety company that makes mobile video surveillance and fleet analytics systems for school buses, transit agencies, commercial fleets, and paratransit operators. Rather than routing customer video and fleet data through a third-party cloud provider, AngelTrax operates its own hosted server infrastructure in a SOC 2 Type II compliant US data center, which the company markets as a security advantage since no third party handles customer footage. The hosted platform supports centralized storage and retrieval of fleet video and transportation data, remote access workflows such as live viewing and downloads, evidence preservation for claims and investigations, and reduced IT burden for customers who would otherwise maintain local servers. AngelTrax's site did not publish the specific city or building housing this infrastructure, nor its founding year or ownership structure, as of the research date, so those are recorded as not published. AngelTrax's data center role in this registry is best understood as an enterprise captive facility built to support a specific product line, comparable in kind though far smaller in scale to the enterprise-operated facilities run by companies like Barclays and Verizon elsewhere in this registry.
